verdict.rationale: ByteAsk is itself an AI coding agent. Its docs show users handing it tasks that it carries out on its own: reading the codebase, editing files, compiling, running tests and returning a diff for review. It can also run a task to completion headlessly via `exec`, and the `/agents` command center groups multiple delegated sessions by status. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that delegated tasks complete reliably in practice.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: ByteAsk opens a full-screen TUI, reads your codebase, edits files, compiles, runs tests, and presents a diff for your review before making permanent changes
`byteask exec` - it runs one task to completion and exits.
/agents opens a command center grouping your agent sessions into needs-input, working, ready and finished.
byteask queue --thread <session> --message "…" sends a message into a running session from another terminal.
